Important privacy note: The repository contains environment variables and hard-coded credentials in several files. This document intentionally uses placeholders such as <API_TOKEN>, <OPENAI_KEY>, and <MONGO_URI> instead of copying any real secret values.

1. How to read this document#

Use this document to understand what each major file does, how the API receives data, how background jobs run, where the data is read from, where it is written back, and how marketplace-specific flows such as bulk enrichment to Myntra or Amazon work.

The service is easiest to understand as a pipeline. A caller sends a requestBody. FastAPI validates it. Short flows run immediately. Long flows are sent to Celery. The business logic reads product data from MongoDB or from the request body, may call AI or image services, may upload processed images to S3, and finally posts the finished result back to a webhook.

When you see a box called OMS in the diagrams, read it as the system that owns catalog tasks and expects webhook updates. The code itself does not define OMS; it just posts JSON payloads to the webhookURL it receives.

i
Static review scope: The documentation was produced from repository inspection. Integration behavior still depends on live secrets, network access, MongoDB data, RabbitMQ/Redis state, S3 buckets, OpenAI/Gemini accounts, and webhook availability.

2. System overview#

The project is a FastAPI + Celery service. FastAPI is the front door. Celery is the background worker system. RabbitMQ is the message broker. Redis stores task states and results. MongoDB stores Rubick OS data such as tasks, taxonomies, org configuration, client rate-limit settings, and usage records. S3 and CloudFront store processed images and created spreadsheets.

The important thing to remember is that most operators mutate the same requestBody object. They read inputColumns, update outputColumns, attach usage, and then call requestToWebhook() if webhookURL is present. For async jobs, the immediate API response is only a Celery task id; the actual business result is normally delivered through the webhook.

3. Repository map#

The repository has one main application package under app/. The most important entry points are app/main.py for HTTP routes, app/worker/functions.py for Celery tasks, app/ml/route.py for synchronous routing wrappers, app/ml/formula.py for generic AI/content flows, and app/ml/marketplace/bulk_detect_enrich_taxonomy.py for the largest marketplace workflow.

Area Main files What to understand
HTTP/API layer app/main.py, app/item.py, app/util.py, app/security.py, app/ratelimiter.py Receives requests, validates operators, builds operandsDict, chooses synchronous execution or Celery execution, and exposes image-link generation.
Celery layer app/worker/celery_app.py, app/worker/functions.py Defines broker/backend, task name prefixes, queues, retry behavior, task progress, and worker task functions.
Generic AI/content layer app/ml/formula.py, app/ml/models.py, app/ml/util.py Builds prompts, calls OpenAI, transforms token usage, posts webhooks, uploads images to S3, and handles generate/enrich/crawl/size-chart/image-pipeline flows.
Marketplace layer app/ml/marketplace/*.py Detects marketplace taxonomy, enriches marketplace templates, handles batch workflows, and applies marketplace-specific rules for Myntra, Amazon, Snapdeal, TataCliq, Ajio, Flipkart, Nykaa, Meesho, and others.
Rubick OS data access app/ml/rubick_os/service.py Central MongoDB access for tasks, taxonomies, org configs, task stages, default taxonomy, order batches, and reusable marketplace data.
Image utilities app/image_processor.py, app/ml/rubick_os/Check_JFIF_image.py, app/ml/ie_automation/* Handles bulk image link generation, JFIF stripping, marketplace image resizing/compression, SKU image sequencing, and S3 uploads.
Quality analysis app/ml/ai_quality_analysis/* CAST pipeline for catalog quality rules such as title, description, legal, size chart, image, spellcheck, and nomenclature checks.
Deployment Dockerfile, docker-compose-local.yml, docker-compose-dev.yml, docker-compose.yml, nginx/, nginx-dev/, rabbitmq.conf Builds the Python 3.10/Poetry container and starts API, workers, Redis, RabbitMQ, Flower, nginx, and certbot services.
Tests tests/marketplace/*.py Focused tests for Amazon image/browse-node behavior and Myntra size enrichment/backfill behavior.

4. Local setup and run commands for dev and prod#

The repository is designed primarily for Docker Compose. The Dockerfile installs Python 3.10, system image-processing libraries, Poetry, and all Poetry dependencies. The compose files then run Hypercorn for FastAPI and Celery for worker processes.

4.1 Prerequisites#

  • Docker and Docker Compose plugin installed. Use docker compose, or docker-compose if your machine still uses the old standalone binary.

  • Python 3.10 if you want to run the API outside Docker.

  • Poetry installed if you want bare-metal local execution.

  • Valid environment values for MongoDB, OpenAI, Myntra OpenAI key if required, Google Translate, AWS/S3, PhotoRoom, crawler, Copyscape, GPTZero, RabbitMQ, and Redis.

  • Network access to the configured MongoDB and external APIs.

4.2 Environment variables to prepare#

Do not paste real values into documentation or git. Put them in a local .env file or in a secret manager. The compose files currently contain many environment entries inline; a safer setup is to replace those values with ${VARIABLE_NAME} references and load them from .env.

Variable Purpose
API_KEY Server API token for protected endpoints. Code currently has a hard-coded comparison in security.py, so align this before relying on env-only auth.
RABBITMQ_BROKER Celery broker URL, for example amqp://user:password@rabbitmq-dev:5672// in Docker or localhost port when running bare-metal.
REDIS_BACKEND Celery result backend URL, for example redis://:password@redis-dev:6379/0 in Docker.
REDIS_QUEUE Queue name. Dev compose uses copilot-queue-dev; prod compose uses copilot-queue.
WORKER_NAME Optional worker/app naming value.
OPEN_AI_API_KEY Default OpenAI key used by app/ml/models.py.
MYNTRA_OPEN_AI_API_KEY Alternate OpenAI key selected for configured org ids in gpt_model().
GOOGLE_TRANSLATION_API_KEY, GOOGLE_TRANSLATION_API_URL Google Translate API configuration for translate flow.
PHOTOROOM_API_KEY PhotoRoom image editing API key.
AWS_BUCKET_NAME, AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_CLOUDFRONT_CDN_LINK S3 and CloudFront configuration for image/file upload flows.
OS_MONGO_URI, OS_DB_NAME Rubick OS MongoDB connection used for tasks, taxonomies, org configs, client keys, usage, and CAST batch lookup.
COPYSCAPE_USERNAME, COPYSCAPE_API_KEY Copyscape plagiarism-check flow.
GPT_ZERO_API_KEY GPTZero AI-text-detection flow.
CRAWL_PRODUCTS_ENDPOINT, CRAWL_PRODUCTS_TOKEN Crawler service called by crawlProducts.
AMAZON_BROWSE_NODE_INDEX_URL plus TTL vars Optional remote static browse-node index and caching behavior for Amazon taxonomy/browse-node resolution.
COPILOT_USAGE_FALLBACK_ORG_ID Fallback org id for usage persistence when orgId is missing or invalid.

4.3 Local development with Docker Compose, no nginx#

This is the most practical local command path because it exposes FastAPI on localhost:8010, RabbitMQ management on localhost:15682, Redis on localhost:6389, and Flower on 127.0.0.1:5550.

Commands
cd rubick-ai-copilot-api

# Build and start all local dev services.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev up -d --build

# Check service status.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev ps

# Watch API and worker logs.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev logs -f fastapi-dev worker-dev

# Health checks.
curl http://localhost:8010/
curl http://localhost:8010/health

# Stop and remove the local dev stack.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev down

Use this mode when you want to develop and test the app without nginx or certificates. The dev queue is copilot-queue-dev. The API container runs Hypercorn with app/app/main:app and binds inside the container to 0.0.0.0:8000.

4.4 Development with nginx/certbot profile#

docker-compose-dev.yml adds nginx and certbot around the same API/worker/Redis/RabbitMQ/Flower pattern. Use it when you need to test reverse-proxy behavior, HTTPS-related config, or dev domains.

Commands
cd rubick-ai-copilot-api

docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yml --profile dev up -d --build
docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yml --profile dev ps
docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yml --profile dev logs -f nginx fastapi-dev worker-dev

docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yml --profile dev down

4.5 Production profile on local machine#

The README only mentions the prod compose profile. It starts reverseproxy, RabbitMQ, Redis, Flower, FastAPI, worker, and certbot. The worker uses copilot-queue and higher concurrency.

Commands
cd rubick-ai-copilot-api

# Same command as README, without sudo unless your Docker install needs it.
docker compose --profile prod up -d --build

# Equivalent explicit file form.
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile prod up -d --build

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile prod ps
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile prod logs -f fastapi worker reverseproxy

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile prod down
i
Prod port-mapping check: docker-compose.yml maps host 8000 to container port 80, but the FastAPI command binds Hypercorn to container port 8000. If http://localhost:8000 does not respond, change the mapping to 8000:8000 or bind Hypercorn to port 80 in the container.

4.6 Bare-metal local run without Docker#

Bare-metal mode is useful when debugging Python code with your IDE. You still need RabbitMQ and Redis somewhere. The easiest hybrid is to run RabbitMQ/Redis from docker-compose-local.yml and run FastAPI/Celery directly on your host.

Commands
cd rubick-ai-copilot-api

# Start only infrastructure containers from the local compose file.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev up -d rabbitmq-dev redis-dev celery-flower-dev

# Python environment.
python3.10 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install poetry
poetry install --no-root

# Example local env values. Replace placeholders with real local-safe values.
export DOCKER=
export RABBITMQ_BROKER='amqp://user:<RABBITMQ_PASSWORD>@localhost:5682//'
export REDIS_BACKEND='redis://:<REDIS_PASSWORD>@localhost:6389/0'
export REDIS_QUEUE='copilot-queue-dev'
export OS_MONGO_URI='<MONGO_URI>'
export OS_DB_NAME='<MONGO_DB_NAME>'
export OPEN_AI_API_KEY='<OPENAI_KEY>'
export MYNTRA_OPEN_AI_API_KEY='<MYNTRA_OPENAI_KEY>'
export AWS_BUCKET_NAME='<BUCKET>'
export AWS_REGION='<REGION>'
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID='<AWS_KEY>'
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY='<AWS_SECRET>'
export AWS_CLOUDFRONT_CDN_LINK='<CLOUDFRONT_PREFIX>'

# Terminal 1: API.
poetry run hypercorn app.main:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8010 --reload

# Terminal 2: worker.
poetry run celery -A app.worker.functions worker -l info -Q copilot-queue-dev --pool=prefork -c 2
i
Import path rule: When DOCKER is unset, task names use app.worker.functions.* and the local worker command uses -A app.worker.functions. In Docker, DOCKER=true and task names use app.app.worker.functions.* because the repository is mounted under /app.

Commands

curl http://localhost:8010/health

# Synchronous preview example. Adjust input shape if your validation branch expects batch-style items.
curl -X POST http://localhost:8010/api/copilot/preview -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'token: <API_TOKEN>' -d '{
"name": "generate",
"operator": "generate",

],

],

{"name": "type", "value": "description"},
{"name": "prompt", "value": "Write a simple ecommerce description."}
],

5. Core request contract and API endpoints#

Almost every flow expects a requestBody dictionary. The exact required fields depend on operator, but the common fields are name, operator, taskId, orgId or brandOrgId, inputColumns, outputColumns, operands, and optional webhookURL.

Field Meaning Used by
name Service/formula name. validateRequestBody() checks it against an allowed list. All /api/copilot routes.
operator The actual operator branch/task name. Often same as name. FastAPI route switch and Celery task name construction.
inputColumns Source data columns. Can contain text, product title, description, attributes, image URLs, image URL arrays, URLs, specs, or nested item payloads. Most operators. Bulk/orderId flows may fetch data from Mongo instead.
outputColumns Target columns to be filled. Operators usually mutate value, type, options, meta, and copilot fields. Most operators and webhook payloads.
operands List of settings objects such as {name: language, value: hi} or model/template/category/etc. Converted into operandsDict before business logic.
operandsDict Dictionary created by convertListToDict(). Not normally sent by caller; created inside FastAPI. All operator functions.
webhookURL Callback URL where final payload is posted. requestToWebhook() in many flows.
usage Token/API usage attached by AI/API flows. Usage persistence and final payload.
brandOrgId Source brand org id for marketplace workflows. Taxonomy/bulk marketplace flows.
marketplaceOrgIds Target marketplace org ids. Current code usually uses the first id. Marketplace flows, usage enrichedFor, image config.
orderId/taskIds Optional batch selectors for Mongo task lookup. Bulk taxonomy/enrichment and CAST order batch.

5.1 Endpoints#

Endpoint Method Execution style Notes
/ GET Immediate Returns {Status: Alive}.
/health GET Immediate Returns a welcome/health message.
/api/copilot/preview POST Synchronous Protected by validate_request. Runs the selected operator directly inside the API process. Useful for quick tests but risky for long jobs.
/api/copilot/client POST Synchronous Protected by client-token auth and rate_limiter_client. Runs directly and removes usage before returning to the client.
/api/copilot/ POST Asynchronous Protected by validate_request. Creates a Celery task and returns celeryTaskId. Result is usually sent to webhookURL.
/api/generate-image-links POST multipart Synchronous thread call Accepts ZIP and/or Excel files, processes images, uploads to S3, and returns output spreadsheet URL.

5.2 Validation behavior#

validateRequestBody() checks that name and operator are in an allowed list. Some taxonomy operators have specific mandatory fields: detectTaxonomy requires skuId, brandOrgId, marketplaceOrgIds; enrichTaxonomy requires skuId and taxonomyId; predictAndEnrichTaxonomy requires skuId, brandOrgId, marketplaceOrgIds; bulkDetectAndEnrichTaxonomy requires brandOrgId and marketplaceOrgIds; customhealthscore requires orgId; brandBulkDetectAndEnrichTaxonomy requires brandOrgId and marketplaceOrgIds.

i
Validation gotcha: The current validation branch treats inputColumns as batch-style items unless orderId is present and checks each item.get("inputColumns"). Some older flat payloads with direct column objects can be rejected even though the operator logic itself expects flat columns.

6. Auth, validation, rate limiting, queues, and usage persistence#

6.1 Authentication#

The API uses a header named token. /api/copilot/preview, /api/copilot/, and /api/generate-image-links call security.validate_request(). /api/copilot/client calls security.validate_client_request() and rate_limiter_client().

validate_client_request() loads client API keys from MongoDB collection client_rate_limiter at import time. That means a key added to Mongo may not become active until the process reloads, unless the code is changed to refresh this list per request or with a cache TTL.

i
Security caution: security.py and ratelimiter.py contain hard-coded secret-like values. For production readiness, move these to environment variables or a secret manager and rotate any values that have been committed.

6.2 Rate limiting#

The basic rate_limiter() function tracks requests per client IP using Redis. The client-specific rate_limiter_client() tracks per token and reads rate_limit and timeout from the client_rate_limiter Mongo collection. However, the Redis connection in ratelimiter.py is hard-coded to an external host and does not use the compose Redis service by default.

6.3 Celery queues and retries#

celery_app.py creates a Celery app using RABBITMQ_BROKER and REDIS_BACKEND. It maps task names to the queue named by REDIS_QUEUE. It also sets late acknowledgements, rejects tasks when workers are lost, tracks started state, and uses Asia/Kolkata timezone.

Most tasks use BaseTaskWithRetry, which retries exceptions up to two times with backoff, except soft/hard time-limit exceptions. The bulk detect/enrich worker task detecttaxonomyenrich has longer time limits because one product group can include image processing, taxonomy detection, enrichment, and webhook posting.

6.4 Usage persistence and webhook posting#

OpenAI and Gemini flows normalize token usage into a usage dictionary. The code persists usage into MongoDB collection copilotusages before webhook posting when possible. requestToWebhook() also tries to persist usage if it has not already been marked as persisted. The payload then goes to webhookURL as JSON.

Usage documents include orgId, userId, taskId, formulaName/formulaId, source, enrichedFor, optional orderId/taskStageId, token counts, service/model, and metadata. Invalid or missing ObjectId fields are replaced with placeholders so that usage is not lost.

8. Common flows used by almost every operator#

8.1 The OpenAI wrapper flow#

gpt_model() is the central OpenAI wrapper. It builds a Responses API input that contains text and optional images. On the first attempt it may send image URLs directly. On retries it tries base64 conversion to reduce image-access failures. It supports plain text, json_object, and json_schema responses.

The function returns two things: the parsed AI result and the normalized usage dictionary. On success or failure it attaches usage to the requestBody and attempts to persist it. It does not retry insufficient_quota errors, but it does retry rate limits with retry-after or exponential backoff.

8.2 Webhook as the final write path#

Most operators do not directly update the OMS database. Instead, they build requestBody["outputColumns"] or requestBody["payload"] and post the entire body to webhookURL. In bulk flows, the webhook output contains a list of task-level results with taskId, taxonomyId, mappedAttributes, and status.

A practical debugging rule is: first check whether outputColumns or payload was filled correctly inside the worker, then check whether requestToWebhook() posted successfully, then check whether OMS accepted the payload.

8.3 Data source priority#

  • Simple preview flows usually read from inputColumns directly.

  • Async flows receive the same requestBody through Celery and then read from inputColumns, operandsDict, and external services.

  • Bulk marketplace flows often ignore the request inputColumns and instead fetch tasks, taxonomies, org configs, and existing marketplace mappings from MongoDB.

  • Image-heavy flows may download from public URLs, Dropbox, Google Drive, or uploaded ZIP/Excel files, then upload processed results to S3/CloudFront.

  • Every flow that calls AI or external APIs should attach usage so that copilotusages can be populated.

9. General content and image operators#

9.1 translate#

Source file: app/ml/translation.py

Translates each input column value into the target language specified by operandsDict["language"].

  • Caller sends inputColumns with text values and an operand named language.

  • googleTranslate() builds q=[all input values], target=<language>, format=text, key=<GOOGLE_TRANSLATION_API_KEY>.

  • It calls GOOGLE_TRANSLATION_API_URL using GET parameters.

  • The translations are written into outputColumns in the same order.

  • If outputColumns contain copilot sub-objects, copilot.value is updated and copilot.status is set false.

  • If webhookURL exists, the updated requestBody is posted back.

  • Data goes from requestBody input text -> Google Translate API -> requestBody outputColumns -> webhook.

9.2 generate#

Source file: app/ml/formula.py: generateFromContent()

Generates a single piece of content, normally description/title/style note/keywords, from provided product content and an optional custom prompt.

  • Read inputColumns and convert each supported type into prompt context.

  • Read operands such as type, prompt, and model; the code defaults to OpenAI gpt-4o for this flow.

  • Build a prompt that says what type of content is required and includes product context.

  • Call gpt_model() with text-only prompt.

  • Write the AI response into outputColumns[0].value and copilot.value when present.

  • Attach usage, persist it, and post webhook if webhookURL exists.

  • Data goes request text -> OpenAI -> created text -> outputColumns/webhook.

9.3 generateBulk#

Source file: app/ml/formula.py: generateBulkFromContent()

Generates multiple output fields in one AI call. It creates a JSON schema from operands such as fields and count.

  • Collect product context from inputColumns.

  • Read operands type, additional-instructions, fields, and count.

  • Build a strict JSON schema for the requested output fields.

  • Call OpenAI through gpt_model() with json_schema.

  • Parse the JSON result and map it back into outputColumns.

  • Attach usage and webhook the request body.

  • Good for creating multiple bullets, titles, descriptions, or structured suggestions in one request.

9.4 enrich#

Source file: app/ml/formula.py: enrichFromImageAndText()

Fills missing attributes using product text and images. It returns both values and confidence where possible.

  • Read inputColumns as known product data and image URLs/image URL arrays.

  • Identify outputColumns that are blank or missing and therefore need enrichment.

  • Resolve Dropbox/Google Drive links where possible; optionally merge images into a labeled grid if operands request it.

  • Build a prompt that asks the model to answer only with JSON: each target attribute gets value and confidence.

  • Call OpenAI, usually gpt-4o-mini, with text and image inputs.

  • Validate/sanitize values, including special handling for age range fields.

  • Write enriched values into outputColumns and copilot metadata, attach usage, and webhook.

  • Data goes product text/images -> OpenAI vision/text -> attribute JSON -> outputColumns/webhook.

  • The flow is used for normal copilot enrichment, not the larger marketplace template enrichment.

9.5 extractSizeChart#

Source file: app/ml/formula.py: generateSizeChart()

Extracts a structured size chart from images and/or text.

  • Collect text and image URLs from inputColumns.

  • Build a prompt asking for category, unit, size_chart, and original_data in JSON.

  • Call OpenAI gpt-4o with images if available.

  • Serialize the returned size chart data into outputColumns.

  • Attach usage and webhook.

  • Data goes product size image/text -> OpenAI vision -> standardized size chart JSON -> outputColumns/webhook.

9.6 crawlProducts#

Source file: app/ml/formula.py: crawlProducts()

Calls an external crawler service for URL input columns and maps scraped fields back to output columns.

  • Find inputColumns of type url.

  • Send taskId and URL list to CRAWL_PRODUCTS_ENDPOINT/scrape-json with bearer token CRAWL_PRODUCTS_TOKEN.

  • Read the returned JSON object/list.

  • For each output column, fill by matching output column names to returned keys.

  • Attach usage-like service metadata including crawler status/error, then webhook.

  • Data goes URL -> crawler service -> scraped JSON -> outputColumns/webhook.

9.7 priceParity#

Source file: app/ml/gemini.py: generateGeminiFromContent()

Estimates an average min/max INR price range for a product title using Vertex AI Gemini.

  • Read title from inputColumns[0].value.

  • Prompt Gemini to return JSON with price.min, price.max, and currency INR.

  • Parse the model text as JSON with fallback to zero range on parse failure.

  • Set outputColumns[0].value to min price, type to range, and options to [min, max, 1].

  • Normalize Gemini usage, persist usage, and webhook.

  • The service-account credential is embedded in code in this repository. Move it to secret storage before production use.

9.8 editImage#

Source file: app/ml/alter.py: editImageAlter()

Edits product images using either PhotoRoom or an Alter API, then stores/returns edited image URLs.

  • Read operands such as template, plan, background, width, height, padding, dpi, shadow, scale, and format.

  • If template is present, use marketplace presets such as amazon, myntra, flipkart, snapdeal, tatacliq, or blinkit.

  • Otherwise choose PhotoRoom when operandsDict["plan"] is photoroom; otherwise call Alter API.

  • For imageurlarray, process comma-separated images and preserve order.

  • Upload PhotoRoom responses to S3 using upload_image_to_s3().

  • Write resulting URLs into outputColumns and webhook.

  • Data goes source image URL -> PhotoRoom/Alter -> S3/CloudFront or returned URL -> outputColumns/webhook.

9.9 healthScore#

Source file: app/ml/health_score.py: calculateHealthScore()

Computes a catalog quality score from title, description, attributes, images, videos, and A+ content.

  • Read title, description, brand, image URLs, video URLs, A+ content, and attributes from inputColumns.

  • Use default thresholds unless requestBody.default_value provides custom thresholds.

  • Score product title sections: character count, junk characters, brand presence, spell check, keyword optimization.

  • Score description sections: character count, junk characters, spell check, keyword optimization, bullets.

  • Score attribute completeness, image count, image quality, video presence, and A+ content presence.

  • Average component scores into outputColumns[0].value and attach detailed scores to outputColumns[0].meta.

  • Webhook the updated requestBody.

  • Data remains mostly local except image URLs are fetched to inspect dimensions.

9.10 customhealthscore and catagory_health_score#

Source file: app/ml/marketplace/custom_health_score.py and app/ml/catagory_health_score.py

customhealthscore batches healthScore across all tasks for an org. catagory_health_score aggregates existing healthScore results into category-level summaries.

  • customhealthscore reads org-specific health score config from orgsconfigs in Mongo.

  • It counts tasks for orgId, fetches them in 100-task batches, formats each task for healthScore, and creates Celery groups.

  • It waits for batch results, then posts a webhook payload containing task ids, health score outputs, total_batch_count, and current_batch_count.

  • catagory_health_score expects inputColumns containing healthScore.meta data and computes averages/medians for category-level outputColumns.

  • customhealthscore is async-only in functions.py. catagory_health_score is preview-only in the current code.

9.11 copyscape and gptZero#

Source file: app/ml/copyscape.py and app/ml/gptZero.py

Adds plagiarism and AI-text-detection results to each input text item.

  • Loop through inputColumns.

  • For Copyscape, POST text to Copyscape API and store parsed response under item["copyscape"].

  • For GPTZero, POST text to GPTZero API and store parsed response under item["gptZero"].

  • Set requestBody.outputColumns to the modified input item list and webhook.

  • Data goes text -> external detection API -> item-level result -> outputColumns/webhook.

9.12 generateRPD#

Source file: app/ml/rpd.py: generateRPDContent()

Fills a design/template JSON object using a mapping from template object ids to input column names.

  • Read operandsDict.template and operandsDict.mapping.

  • Create a lookup of template json.objects by object id.

  • Create a lookup of input columns by name.

  • For each mapping entry, copy input value into either template object src for image types or text for text fields.

  • Write the final template to outputColumns[0].raw and copilot.value, then webhook.

  • Data goes input columns -> template object JSON -> outputColumns/webhook.

9.13 intelCopilot#

Source file: app/ml/intel_copilot.py: predictCopilotMeta()

Analyzes product and competitor images to suggest predicted shots, missing shots, missing images, and Pinterest trend keywords.

  • Read current product title and images from inputColumns.

  • Read competitor images from requestBody.competitors.

  • Download/convert images to base64 and resize for model input.

  • Use image embeddings to identify competitor images not already represented by product images.

  • Call Gemini with product images and a system prompt for shot prediction and trend keywords.

  • Build four output columns: Predicted Shots, Missing Shots, Missing Images, Pinterest Predict.

  • Attach Gemini usage and webhook.

9.14 predictshopifycategory#

Source file: app/ml/shopify_catagory_prediction.py

Predicts a Shopify category tree for a product using an OpenAI Assistant id and Shopify_category.json as allowed values.

  • Expect inputColumns[0] to be a dict with image and name.

  • Build prompt text from product name.

  • Load allowed category values from Shopify_category.json.

  • Call Assistant(prompt, assistant_id).

  • If response category tree is allowed, append it to outputColumns and webhook.

  • Current models.py Assistant helper references a variable named client that is not defined in the inspected file, so this flow likely needs a code fix before use.

10. Marketplace taxonomy and enrichment flows#

Marketplace flows are where the service becomes much more than a simple AI prompt. These flows combine source brand product data, MongoDB task/taxonomy records, org-specific knowledgebase mappings, marketplace template rules, image processing, and AI-created values.

10.1 Important marketplace vocabulary#

Term Meaning
Brand org The org that owns the source product data. In requests this is often brandOrgId or orgId.
Marketplace org The target marketplace org, such as Myntra, Amazon, Ajio, Flipkart, Nykaa, Snapdeal, TataCliq, Meesho. In requests this is marketplaceOrgIds, usually a list but the code mainly uses the first id.
Task A MongoDB tasks document. Source tasks contain brand attributes. Marketplace tasks can contain mapped marketplace attributes.
Default taxonomy A fallback taxonomy for a marketplace. Bulk flows select source tasks still mapped to the default taxonomy and then detect/enrich a better target taxonomy.
Taxonomy template A marketplace-specific list of attributes, allowed values, mandatory flags, image fields, and recommended browse node fields.
mappedAttributes The output dictionary sent back to OMS for a marketplace task. Keys are marketplace template attributes.
Knowledgebase Org config mapping rules in orgsconfigs, used to copy/override brand info, categories, and attributes into enriched marketplace data.
Reusable enriched task An already-enriched marketplace task in the same product/style group. Bulk flow can copy it to sibling variants and only adjust variant-specific fields.

10.3 Single detectTaxonomy flow#

detectTaxonomy#

Source file: app/ml/marketplace/detect_taxonomy.py

Predicts the best marketplace taxonomy for one SKU/task.

  • Request provides skuId, brandOrgId, and marketplaceOrgIds.

  • Code fetches the task from Mongo and extracts product text attributes and main image.

  • Code fetches all taxonomies for the target marketplace org.

  • Prompt asks OpenAI gpt-4o-mini to choose one taxonomy from the list.

  • If predicted taxonomy is found, requestBody.payload is set with skuId, taxonomyId, taxonomyName, and marketplaceOrgIds.

  • Wrapper posts webhook if used through Celery detect_taxonomy wrapper.

  • Data goes Mongo task + taxonomy list -> OpenAI classifier -> payload/webhook.

10.4 Single enrichTaxonomy flow#

enrichTaxonomy#

Source file: app/ml/marketplace/enrich_taxonomy.py

Maps and enriches one SKU into a known marketplace taxonomy template.

  • Request provides skuId, taxonomyId, and marketplaceOrgIds.

  • Code fetches the source task and taxonomy template from Mongo.

  • Code reads orgsconfigs for knowledgebase entries under apiKeys[marketplaceOrgId].

  • Known mapped fields, brand information, and image columns are filled first.

  • Remaining template fields are sent to OpenAI with allowed values and product context.

  • The returned JSON is sanitized against select/multiselect allowed values.

  • requestBody.payload is set with skuId, taxonomyId, taxonomyName, marketplaceOrgIds, and mappedAttributes.

  • Wrapper posts webhook.

  • This is a legacy/smaller path. The bulk file contains newer shared logic and more marketplace-specific handling.

10.5 predictAndEnrichTaxonomy flow#

predictAndEnrichTaxonomy#

Source file: app/ml/marketplace/generate_marketplace_template.py

Runs taxonomy detection first and then enrichment for the predicted taxonomy.

  • Call predict_taxonomy(requestBody).

  • If payload contains a taxonomyId, copy it into requestBody["taxonomyId"].

  • Call map_and_enrich_taxonomy(requestBody).

  • Return the enriched requestBody and post webhook in the wrapper.

  • Data goes SKU -> taxonomy detection -> taxonomy enrichment -> webhook.

11. Bulk marketplace flows, including Myntra and Amazon#

bulkDetectAndEnrichTaxonomy is the central high-volume marketplace workflow. It does not just enrich one payload from inputColumns. It uses brandOrgId, marketplaceOrgIds, orderId/taskIds, default taxonomy, task grouping, Celery groups, reusable mappings, and marketplace-specific finalization.

11.1 Bulk request acceptance: from API to worker groups#

  • OMS/client posts a request to /api/copilot/ with operator bulkDetectAndEnrichTaxonomy, brandOrgId, marketplaceOrgIds, optional orderId, optional taskIds, and webhookURL.

  • FastAPI validates brandOrgId and marketplaceOrgIds, creates operandsDict, and sends Celery task bulkDetectAndEnrichTaxonomy.

  • The bulk task reads the first marketplaceOrgId and calls get_default_taxonomy(marketplaceOrgId).

  • It finds product ids or style group ids where source tasks are still mapped to the marketplace default taxonomy. If the brand org is one of the configured Myntra grouping brand orgs, tasks are grouped by styleGroupId; otherwise usually by productId.

  • It checks active Celery tasks and Redis to avoid duplicate product groups.

  • It creates a Celery group of detecttaxonomyenrich tasks. Each task receives the original requestBody plus product_id, default taxonomy id, brand org id, marketplace org id, request type, isShopify flag, and a batch id.

  • The immediate response is {status: request accepted}. Real enriched data is sent later by webhook from detect_taxonomy_enrich().

11.2 Shopify-style product group flow#

In the main Shopify path, detect_taxonomy_enrich() fetches all source tasks for one product/style group. If isShopify is true, group_by_variant() groups variants by non-size options so similar variants can share enrichment while preserving size-specific fields.

  • Fetch group tasks from Mongo using get_all_task_by_parent_id().

  • Flatten the first task into product_data using flat_json(). It extracts product fields and an images list.

  • Determine which tasks are still pending for the target marketplace/default taxonomy.

  • Look for a reusable enriched marketplace task. If found, copy its mappedAttributes as a seed.

  • If no reusable mapping exists, detect marketplace taxonomy with _taxonomy_from_request_operands() override or detect_taxonomy_base().

  • Fetch taxonomy details and existing mapped marketplace data if present.

  • Run enrich_data() to produce base mapped attributes.

  • Infer numeric source maps and size source maps from the seed task so sibling variants keep their own prices/sizes/measurements.

  • For each pending task, copy base enrichment, apply variant-specific numeric/size values, process external image links, finalize marketplace-specific rules, and append a result object.

  • Set requestBody.outputColumns to a list of task-level results, attach usage/stage breakdown, add batchId, and post webhook.

11.3 Brand fallback/path#

The same worker also has a Brand path. It fetches one task by task id, flattens brand attributes, detects taxonomy, enriches, applies marketplace rules, and posts a single-result output. Some exceptions in Shopify processing can fall back to this Brand path.

11.4 Where data goes in bulk marketplace flow#

Stage Data read from Data written to / sent to
Request acceptance HTTP requestBody from OMS/client Celery task queue and immediate accepted response
Default taxonomy lookup Mongo taxonomies collection default_taxonomy_id variable used for task selection
Source task selection Mongo tasks collection filtered by brand org, default taxonomy, optional orderId/taskIds product/style group list and per-group Celery tasks
Product flattening Mongo task attributes and mappedTaxonomyIds product_data dict with title/specs/options/images
Taxonomy detection product_data, marketplace taxonomy names, knowledgebase subscribed categories, Amazon browse index if relevant detected taxonomy name/id and usage stage data
Template enrichment target taxonomy attributes/allowed values, product_data, images, mapped marketplace data enriched_data dictionary
Knowledgebase mapping orgsconfigs.apiKeys[marketplaceOrgId] overridden/copied brand/category/attribute values in enriched_data
Image processing product image URLs or external image links S3/CloudFront URLs in mappedAttributes
Variant finalization source task-specific price/size fields and seed enriched_data one mappedAttributes dict per task
Webhook all_data_processed list and request metadata webhookURL POST to OMS

11.5 Myntra bulk enrichment flow#

Myntra is special because marketplace-size fields are heavily variant-specific. The seed enriched result may be created from one variant, but sibling variants need their own Standard Size, Brand Size, measurements, vendor codes, and sometimes MRP values. The code handles this with size-source inference and a Myntra size mapping catalog.

  • Source brand tasks are grouped by styleGroupId for configured Myntra brand org ids. This lets all variants of a style share one enrichment seed.

  • The first variant is flattened and enriched against the Myntra taxonomy template.

  • Images are processed with process_image() into S3/CloudFront under Image-dump/<date>/<brandOrgId>/<marketplaceOrgId>.

  • The code infers which source key produced Standard Size or equivalent target size fields. For example, Size, Product_Size, Shirt Size Value, or Size In Alphabet can map to Standard Size when allowed by taxonomy options.

  • For each sibling variant, copied size fields are cleared and then restored from that sibling task, not from the seed variant.

  • finalize_myntra_variant_size_attributes() uses articleType, AgeGroup, Standard Size, source attributes, and myntra_bulk_size_mapping.json to fill measurements such as chest/shoulder/waist where configured.

  • MRP-like fields are rounded using convert_price(). Schema aliases are applied so alternative field names still land in the correct Myntra fields.

  • The final mappedAttributes are posted for each task id in outputColumns.

Example: if the seed product is size M and a sibling is size XL, the LLM output may initially contain M. The finalization layer should replace Standard Size and size-derived measurements with XL-specific values before webhook posting.

11.6 Amazon bulk enrichment flow#

Amazon is special because Recommended Browse Nodes and image URL fields require dedicated logic. The code tries to avoid sending browse node fields blindly through the main LLM enrichment call and instead resolves them using a candidate index, taxonomy options, scoring, and optional LLM reranking.

  • detect_taxonomy_base() may first ask the LLM for a compact product_type from source title/description/article type.

  • The Amazon browse-node matcher loads candidates from a local/static JSON index or CDN URL and combines them with taxonomy Recommended Browse Node options.

  • Candidates are filtered and scored using product type tokens, source product concept text, taxonomy context, template root/context statistics, supported/unsupported leaf evidence, and audience adjustments.

  • When a high-confidence direct candidate exists, it is used without the expensive taxonomy classifier. Otherwise the code falls back to LLM taxonomy detection and later browse-node resolution.

  • The resolved browse node is assigned into Recommended Browse Nodes fields and enforced again during finalization so copied/reusable data does not keep stale browse nodes.

  • Images are assigned to Amazon-specific URL fields: Main Image URL for the first image and Other Image URL_1 through Other Image URL_8 for the rest. Fields such as Swatch Image URL, Main Image Location, and Other Image Location_* are cleared.

Data goes from brand product text/images -> product type extraction -> browse-node candidate index/taxonomy -> scoring/rerank -> enriched Amazon mappedAttributes -> webhook to OMS.

11.7 Other marketplace special cases#

Marketplace Special behavior seen in code
Snapdeal If Common or Generic Name of the commodity is blank, knowledgebase finalization can fill it with taxonomy name. Detection fallback contains a casual trouser heuristic for joggers/cargo/baggy/chinos terms.
Meesho Taxonomy detection has fuzzy token/path matching fallback when model output is not exactly in the taxonomy list.
TataCliq Certain image fields are joined into one field with IMAGE PRIORITY = 1, and configured empty attributes can be set blank.
Flipkart Shares image processing style with URL-list processing and has image-field joining logic similar to TataCliq in the enrichment branch.
Ajio/Nykaa Uses process_image_url_list() for marketplace-configured resizing/compression and S3 upload.
Coyu Listed in marketplace org map; specific custom logic is less prominent than Myntra/Amazon/Snapdeal in inspected code.

11.8 Reusable enriched task flow#

If a product/style group already contains a marketplace task that is not on the default taxonomy and has meaningful mapped attributes, the bulk worker can reuse it. This prevents repeated LLM calls and keeps consistent marketplace data across variants.

  • Find a reusable task in the group for the target marketplace.

  • Flatten its mappedAttributes into reusable enriched data.

  • Get the taxonomy id/name from the reusable task.

  • For Amazon, re-resolve browse nodes when missing or stale.

  • Infer numeric and standard-size source maps from reusable data.

  • For each pending task, copy reusable data, apply task-specific price/size/image finalization, and append success output.

12. Image processing flows#

12.1 /api/generate-image-links#

This endpoint is different from /api/copilot/. It accepts multipart uploads: a ZIP file and/or Excel files plus marketplace, optional ratio, width, and height. It saves files under temp/<job_id>, processes them in a thread, uploads processed images and output.xlsx to S3, and returns URLs.

  • ZIP mode: extract uploaded ZIP under temp/<job_id>/imgs, ignore __MACOSX and dot files, convert each valid image, upload folder to S3, and produce rows with SHEET, sku, path 1..20.

  • Excel mode: read each spreadsheet, require sku and img_url 1 columns, fix Dropbox links, download images from URL columns, convert images, upload to S3, and produce output rows.

  • Conversion uses Pillow. It validates ratio if ratio/width/height are provided, converts to JPEG, compresses if too large, and tries to increase size if below marketplace minimum where configured.

  • The final output.xlsx is uploaded to BAU/imgs_final/<job_id>/output.xlsx. If ratio validation fails, the endpoint may also upload imgs_final.zip and return a manual intervention message.

Marketplace size limits in image_processor.py include Myntra, Ajio, Flipkart, Nykaa, Amazon, and TataCliq. app/ml/util.py also contains a MARKETPLACE_CONFIG used by the marketplace enrichment image URL processing functions with target dimensions and aspect ratios.

12.2 jfifimagecheck#

jfifimagecheck receives inputColumns where each item should include brand_org_id, marketplaceOrgIds, and image as a list. It streams images, converts them to JPEG, strips the JFIF header if found, compresses large images, uploads to S3/CloudFront, and stores Processed_image in the output.

12.3 marketplaceImageTemplate / imagePipeline#

The IE automation image pipeline receives one SKU with images, creates a temporary workspace, optionally downloads VIT/reference assets, downloads SKU images, categorizes images, applies jewellery sharpening, fixes dimensions, sequences apparel shots, adds missing/additional angle handling, processes shoe top/bottom views, merges shoe images, exports final images, uploads them to S3, and writes final CDN URLs into outputColumns.

The async Celery task is named marketplaceImageTemplate. The preview route has a branch named imagePipeline, but validation does not currently list imagePipeline. The implementation should align naming before using the preview branch.

13. CAST quality-analysis flow#

CAST stands for catalog quality checks. The code under app/ml/ai_quality_analysis runs a config-driven pipeline that validates title, description, attributes, size chart, legal/compliance fields, image rules, spellcheck, nomenclature, and additional checks. It supports at least Myntra and TataCliq; other organizations are rejected by the inspected pipeline.

  • run_pipeline_from_request() deep-copies the request and builds a root_request containing orgId, formulaId, formulaName, source, operator, and operands.

  • It resolves organization from operands named Marketplace, then config default, then source fallback. Only myntra and tatacliq are supported in the inspected code.

  • It loads config.yaml and flattens organization-specific thresholds, prompts, input mappings, and applicable analysis rules.

  • If orderId is present, it fetches tasks from Mongo in batches of 200 and builds one per-task request body for each task. If orderId is absent, it builds documents from request inputColumns.

  • Each document is processed by analyzers: title, description, attribute, general, size chart, legal compliance, country of origin checks, image, spellcheck, nomenclature, and additional checks.

  • Results are converted into outputColumns by PayloadOutputHandler and posted to the webhook per SKU/task.

  • The Celery task castChecks updates progress to 5% then 100%, while the pipeline itself can update phases such as NORMALIZE_PAYLOAD and EXEC_RULES.

The CAST README in the repository explains individual checks such as title length, title unicode characters, article type match, list view title length, description bullet points, specification count, material and care, size chart availability, size chart standard sizes, country of origin, manufacturer/importer/packer details, and more.

15. How to add or debug an operator#

15.1 Adding a new operator#

  • Add the operator name to List_operator in app/util.py.

  • If the operator has mandatory request fields, add them to validate_taxonomy_requestBody() or create a new validation helper.

  • Add a business function under app/ml/ or the appropriate subpackage.

  • Add a wrapper in app/ml/route.py if the operator should work synchronously through /api/copilot/preview or /api/copilot/client.

  • Add a branch in app/main.py copilotPreview() for sync usage.

  • Add a Celery task in app/worker/functions.py if it should run asynchronously.

  • Add a task route entry in app/worker/celery_app.py for both local and Docker task-name prefixes.

  • Make sure docker-compose env vars include any new external API keys or endpoints.

  • Attach usage where relevant and call requestToWebhook() with a clear output shape.

  • Add tests under tests/ for deterministic helper logic.

15.2 Debug checklist#

Symptom Where to check first Common cause
400 No such operator/name app/util.py List_operator operator/name not listed or mismatch between preview name and worker task name.
400 received empty inputColumns app/util.py validation Payload is flat legacy columns but current validation expects batch-style nested items unless orderId is present.
Async task never runs RabbitMQ UI, Flower, worker logs, REDIS_QUEUE Queue mismatch, wrong DOCKER task prefix, worker not consuming the same queue.
Task retries/fails quickly worker logs and Celery result traceback External API key missing, Mongo unreachable, image URL download failure, model quota/rate-limit.
Webhook not received requestToWebhook() logs and webhookURL value Webhook endpoint error, timeout, payload rejected by OMS.
Usage missing copilotusages collection and logs from copilot_usage_persistence.py No usage attached, zero-token usage skipped, invalid Mongo credentials, duplicate mark behavior.
Bulk outputs same size for all variants Myntra size source map/finalization tests Variant-specific size source not inferred or allowed values do not contain source size.
Amazon images in wrong columns _assign_amazon_image_fields() tests Image field names not matching expected Main Image URL / Other Image URL_n fields.
Prod API not reachable on 8000 docker-compose.yml fastapi ports and command Host maps 8000:80 while Hypercorn listens on 8000 in container.
Client token recently added but still unauthorized security.py import-time Api_list Client API key list is loaded only when process starts.

16. Testing, troubleshooting, and known risks#

16.1 Tests found in repository#

The tests are focused on deterministic marketplace helper behavior. They do not cover full integration with live Mongo, OpenAI, S3, or RabbitMQ.

Commands
cd rubick-ai-copilot-api
poetry run pytest

# Focused marketplace tests.
poetry run pytest tests/marketplace/test_amazon_image_fields.py
poetry run pytest tests/marketplace/test_myntra_size_enrichment.py
poetry run pytest tests/marketplace/test_myntra_standard_size_source_backfill.py

  • test_amazon_image_fields.py checks Amazon browse-node/image-field helper behavior.

  • test_myntra_size_enrichment.py checks catalog-driven Myntra size enrichment behavior.

  • test_myntra_standard_size_source_backfill.py checks variant-specific Standard Size source inference and backfill behavior.

16.2 Known risks and code smells from static review#

Risk / issue Impact Suggested fix
Secrets and private credentials appear in repository files and compose files. Credential leakage, unauthorized usage, production security risk. Rotate exposed values, remove from git history where appropriate, load secrets from env/secret manager.
security.py compares token to a hard-coded value instead of API_KEY env. Changing API_KEY env may not affect auth; secret rotation is harder. Use os.environ.get("API_KEY") or proper secret storage.
ratelimiter.py uses a hard-coded external Redis host/password. Local compose Redis is bypassed; security and portability risk. Use REDIS_URL env and configure per environment.
docker-compose.yml maps fastapi port 8000:80 while Hypercorn binds 8000. Prod profile may not expose API correctly. Use 8000:8000 or bind Hypercorn to 80.
Preview route has imagePipeline/castPipeline branches, but validation list has marketplaceImageTemplate/castChecks instead. Preview calls can be rejected before reaching branch. Align operator names across validation, main route, worker, docs, and client.
hintEnrich/enrichImageText are allowed/routed but no active implementation was found. Requests may create unresolved tasks or 400 behavior. Remove legacy names or implement tasks/routes.
Assistant() in models.py references client, which was not defined in the inspected file. predictshopifycategory likely fails at runtime. Use OPENAI_DEFAULT_CLIENT or create a correctly named client.
get_product_id_celery() reads args[0] for detecttaxonomyenrich even though product_id is args[1]. Duplicate-product prevention may not work as intended. Read args[1] after confirming Celery arg serialization.
getAllTaxonomies() appears to check built-in id instead of org_id. Missing org_id validation may not fire. Change condition to if not org_id.
Legacy enrich_taxonomy.py references names that may be missing/undefined in the file. Single enrichTaxonomy may fail depending on code path. Prefer bulk shared logic or fix imports/constants/tests.
Api_list for client auth/rate limit loaded at import time. New client keys/rate limits require app restart. Add cache refresh or DB lookup with TTL.
Large sync preview jobs can block API workers. Slow user-facing requests and timeouts. Use /api/copilot/ async endpoint for image, bulk, and CAST jobs.

16.3 Practical troubleshooting commands#

Commands
# Compose status.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev ps

# API logs.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev logs -f fastapi-dev

# Worker logs.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev logs -f worker-dev

# RabbitMQ management UI.
# Open http://localhost:15682 and check queues, messages ready/unacked, consumers.

# Flower UI.
# Open http://127.0.0.1:5550 and inspect active, failed, retried, and succeeded tasks.

# Check that the worker is consuming the queue you send to.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev exec worker-dev poetry run celery -A app.app.worker.functions inspect active_queues

# Print relevant env values inside fastapi without exposing secret values.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev exec fastapi-dev python -c "import os; print('queue=', os.environ.get('REDIS_QUEUE')); print('docker=', os.environ.get('DOCKER'))"

# Inspect active Celery tasks.
docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml --profile dev exec worker-dev poetry run celery -A app.app.worker.functions inspect active

17. Appendix: glossary#

Term Meaning in this repository
requestBody The JSON object that enters the API and is carried through route functions, Celery tasks, LLM calls, outputColumns, usage, and webhook callbacks.
inputColumns Source data from OMS/client. Despite the name, it can contain text fields, images, URLs, task metadata, or nested objects.
outputColumns Where the API writes the created/enriched result before returning or sending the webhook.
operands Settings sent by the caller, such as prompt, model, marketplace, type, width, height, template, and additional instructions.
taxonomy Marketplace-specific category/template definition. It tells the system which attributes are required and what values are allowed.
mappedAttributes Final marketplace-ready key/value attributes created for a SKU/task.
webhookURL Callback endpoint where completed async task results are posted.
usage Token/service usage metadata attached to the result and persisted into Mongo.
taskId Rubick OS/OMS task document id. Bulk marketplace flows usually operate over many taskIds.
orderId Batch/order identifier used to find many tasks in Mongo.
styleGroupId / parentProductId Grouping keys used to process product variants together, especially for Myntra size enrichment.
Celery queue RabbitMQ queue consumed by worker containers. Dev queue is usually copilot-queue-dev; prod queue is usually copilot-queue.

17.1 Minimal sample: async bulk marketplace request#

JSON
{
"name": "bulkDetectAndEnrichTaxonomy",
"payload": {
"brandOrgId": "<brand org id>",
"marketplaceOrgIds": ["<marketplace org id, e.g. Amazon/Myntra org id>"],
"orderId": "<optional order id>",
"taskIds": ["<optional task id 1>", "<optional task id 2>"],
"webhookURL": "https://<your callback endpoint>",
"operands": [
{"name": "isShopify", "value": "false"},
{"name": "category", "value": "<optional taxonomy/category override>"}
]
}
}

The request enters /api/copilot/. FastAPI validates it, creates a Celery task, and returns celeryTaskId immediately. The bulk scheduler then creates many detecttaxonomyenrich tasks. Each worker writes mappedAttributes for one task/group and posts results to webhookURL.

17.2 Minimal sample: sync generate request#

JSON
{
"name": "generate",
"payload": {
"inputColumns": [
{"name": "title", "value": "Men blue cotton casual shirt"}
],
"outputColumns": [
{"name": "description", "type": "description"}
],
"operands": [
{"name": "type", "value": "description"},
{"name": "model", "value": "gpt-4o-mini"},
{"name": "prompt", "value": "Write a simple ecommerce description."}
],
"webhookURL": "https://<optional callback>"
}
}

This request can go to /api/copilot/preview for synchronous testing or /api/copilot/ for asynchronous processing. In both cases, the output is written to outputColumns[0].value.

17.4 Image output requirements by marketplace#

Marketplace Target width x height Max size Notes
Myntra 1080 x 1440 1000 KB 3:4 aspect ratio. Bulk image path uses Image-dump/date/brand/Myntra.
Amazon 1500 x 1500 2000 KB Square image. Bulk enrich assigns Main Image URL and Other Image URL fields.
Ajio 2000 x 2500 1000 KB 4:5 aspect ratio.
Nykaa 1500 x 2000 2000 KB Processed via image URL list helper.
TataCliq 1080 x 1440 800 KB Some flows join image URLs and set IMAGE PRIORITY=1.
Flipkart 200 x 1000 1000 KB Image processing helper used in bulk enrich.
Snapdeal Marketplace helper 1000 KB target in several helpers Uses generic name/category fallback and image dump path.

17.5 Onboarding checklist#

  • Start by running docker-compose-local.yml with the dev profile. Confirm / and /health return responses.

  • Open Flower and RabbitMQ management before testing async tasks. They make queue issues much easier to understand.

  • Use /api/copilot/preview only for small synchronous jobs. Use /api/copilot/ for bulk/image/CAST jobs.

  • Trace a request in this order: main.py -> util.py validation -> route.py or Celery -> ml module -> models/util usage -> webhook.

  • For marketplace bulk bugs, first identify marketplaceOrgId, brandOrgId, orderId/taskIds, default taxonomy, grouping key, and final mappedAttributes.

  • For image bugs, check whether the image came from ZIP/Excel, Dropbox/GDrive, product source images, or AI pipeline output.

  • Never commit real credentials. Use .env files ignored by git or a proper secret manager.
